metadata.scope_note: Industry-source citations grounding the prevalence and impact claims for each of the 12 risk scenarios, plus the legal and regulatory primary sources (GDPR, EU AI Act, Article 29 WP guidance, ENISA algorithmic-decision-making guidance) cited in the project's regulatory-mapping discussion. Sources are major annual cybersecurity reports, a small number of academic references, and four primary regulatory texts. Where a specific quantitative claim or statutory provision is cited, the page, article, or section is recorded so a reader can verify it; numbers may shift across annual report editions and should be re-verified against the source PDF, but the primary regulatory texts are stable Official Journal references.
metadata.verification_note: Citations were assembled from publicly-available report tables of contents and high-level findings as of May 2026. Before any external publication, verify each direct numerical claim against the source PDF and update the page/section reference if the source has issued a revised edition.

verizon_dbir_2025.author: Verizon Business
verizon_dbir_2025.title: 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report
verizon_dbir_2025.notes: Annual analysis of confirmed data breaches; widely-cited industry baseline. Section structure stable across editions: Results & Analysis, Industries, Regional Analysis, Incident Classification Patterns, Conclusion.

mandiant_mtrends_2025.author: Mandiant (Google Cloud)
mandiant_mtrends_2025.title: M-Trends 2025 Special Report
mandiant_mtrends_2025.notes: Annual incident-response retrospective covering attacker dwell time, initial-access vectors, and lateral-movement patterns. Reports global median dwell time, regional breakdowns, and per-sector attack patterns.

microsoft_mddr_2024.author: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
microsoft_mddr_2024.title: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2024
microsoft_mddr_2024.notes: Annual threat-intelligence report covering nation-state activity, identity attacks, ransomware trends, and cloud security incidents.

ibm_codb_2024.author: IBM Security and Ponemon Institute
ibm_codb_2024.title: Cost of a Data Breach Report 2024
ibm_codb_2024.notes: Annual quantitative breach-impact study based on interviews with 600+ organisations. Reports cost per record, time-to-identify and contain, attack vectors, mitigating controls.

enisa_etl_2024.author: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA)
enisa_etl_2024.title: ENISA Threat Landscape 2024
enisa_etl_2024.notes: Annual EU-focused threat landscape covering insider threats, supply chain, ransomware, and AI-enabled attacks. Maps findings to NIS2 risk-management measures.

acfe_rtn_2024.author: Association of Certified Fraud Examiners
acfe_rtn_2024.title: Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations
acfe_rtn_2024.notes: Biennial study of occupational fraud cases. Most authoritative public source on insider-fraud schemes including segregation-of-duties bypass and asset misappropriation.

cisa_insider_threat_guide.author: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
cisa_insider_threat_guide.title: Insider Threat Mitigation Guide
cisa_insider_threat_guide.notes: U.S. federal guidance on insider-threat detection and mitigation. Covers behavioural indicators, technical controls, and incident-response patterns.

gartner_uemba_2024.author: Gartner Research
gartner_uemba_2024.title: Market Guide for User and Entity Behavior Analytics
gartner_uemba_2024.notes: Gartner's coverage of UEBA shifted from a Magic Quadrant to a Market Guide format; the Market Guide remains the canonical industry reference for UEBA capabilities and vendor positioning.

glasser_lindauer_2013.author: Glasser, J. and Lindauer, B.
glasser_lindauer_2013.title: Bridging the Gap: A Pragmatic Approach to Generating Insider Threat Data
glasser_lindauer_2013.notes: The CERT Insider Threat Test Dataset paper — the closest publicly-available analogue to a real PAM corpus. Cited as background for why a synthetic PAM corpus is needed.

raffel_t5_2020.author: Raffel, C. et al.
raffel_t5_2020.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
raffel_t5_2020.notes: T5 / Flan-T5 architecture paper. Cited as the augmentation backbone used by `code/generator/llm_augment.py` in HuggingFace mode.

shostack_threat_modeling_2014.author: Shostack, A.
shostack_threat_modeling_2014.title: Threat Modeling: Designing for Security
shostack_threat_modeling_2014.notes: Canonical STRIDE reference. Already cited in §3.5 for STRIDE methodology.

mitre_attck_v15.author: MITRE Corporation
mitre_attck_v15.title: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix v15.1
mitre_attck_v15.notes: Tactics-and-techniques knowledge base for adversary behaviour. Already cited in §3.5 and threat_model.json.

gdpr_2016.author: European Parliament and Council
gdpr_2016.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation
gdpr_2016.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union L 119, 4 May 2016
gdpr_2016.notes: Cited in §3.6 (control-ID mapping in `code/regulatory_map.json`) and §11 (Articles 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e), 22, 32, and Recital 47 — the proportionality, data-minimisation, storage-limitation, and human-oversight provisions central to the ethical engagement with privileged-access monitoring).

eu_ai_act_2024.author: European Parliament and Council
eu_ai_act_2024.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
eu_ai_act_2024.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union L 1689, 12 July 2024
eu_ai_act_2024.notes: Annex III §4 classifies AI systems intended to evaluate worker behaviour or performance as high-risk, triggering Articles 9-17 (risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight, post-market monitoring). Article 14's human-oversight obligation maps onto this project's analyst-in-the-loop verdict-before-action design.

article29wp_2017.author: Article 29 Data Protection Working Party
article29wp_2017.title: Opinion 2/2017 on data processing at work (WP 249)
article29wp_2017.notes: Cited in §11. Endorses automated tools for monitoring high-risk privileged-user activities (administrative access, data extraction, configuration changes) provided that scope is limited to those activities and workers are informed. The authoritative pre-EDPB guidance on workplace monitoring proportionality, still cited as the reference document for new deployments.

enisa_adm_2020.author: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA)
enisa_adm_2020.title: Algorithmic Decision-Making and Personal Data — Technical Guidance
enisa_adm_2020.notes: Cited in §11 as the authoritative reference for engineering practices that operationalise data minimisation, storage limitation, and pseudonymisation across pipeline stages of an algorithmic decision-making system processing personal data.

nis2_2022.author: European Parliament and Council
nis2_2022.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 — NIS2 Directive on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union
nis2_2022.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union L 333, 27 December 2022
nis2_2022.notes: Cited in §3.6 (control-ID mapping in `code/regulatory_map.json`) and §1.5 (essential-entity / important-entity designation, Article 21(2)(b) incident handling, Article 21(2)(j) multi-factor authentication / continuous authentication). The regulatory anchor that makes a behavioural-analytics PAM layer a direct implementation of an EU-mandated risk-management measure for critical-infrastructure operators.

bamford_2014.author: Bamford, J.
bamford_2014.title: Edward Snowden: The untold story
bamford_2014.notes: Cited in §1.5. Long-form reportage on the Snowden case treated as the canonical public reference for the technical contours of the disclosure (privileged access, session-recording absence, post-hoc forensic reconstruction). Bamford is the standard public-domain reference; PERSEREC studies are the parallel cleared-environment academic body but most are restricted distribution.

cisa_solarwinds_2021.author: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), FBI, and ODNI
cisa_solarwinds_2021.title: Joint Statement on the Russian SVR-attributed compromise of SolarWinds Orion (UNC2452 / NOBELIUM)
cisa_solarwinds_2021.notes: Authoritative public reference for the SolarWinds Orion supply-chain compromise (December 2020). The technical advisory documents the privileged-AD post-exploitation phase that maps onto the same telemetry surface the project's detectors evaluate.

dora_2022.author: European Parliament and Council
dora_2022.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 — Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
dora_2022.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union L 333, 27 December 2022
dora_2022.notes: Cited in Appendix E. Article 9(2)(c) requires explicit monitoring of user activities for ICT third-party-risk-management purposes — the financial-services-sector overlay on top of GDPR and NIS2 in the EU regime.

hipaa_security_rule.author: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
hipaa_security_rule.title: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C — Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic Protected Health Information)
hipaa_security_rule.notes: Cited in Appendix E. §164.312(b) audit-controls obligation requires healthcare covered entities and business associates to record and examine activity in information systems containing electronic protected health information — maps cleanly onto privileged-session monitoring.

sox_pcaob_2007.author: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB)
sox_pcaob_2007.title: Auditing Standard No. 5 (now Audit Standard 2201) — An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sox_pcaob_2007.notes: Cited in Appendix E. The implementing audit standard for the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (15 U.S.C. §7262) requirement to test operating effectiveness of internal controls over financial reporting. For privileged administrators of general-ledger systems, the §6 detector capability provides direct evidence.

nist_csf_2024.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
nist_csf_2024.title: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29)
nist_csf_2024.notes: Cited in Appendix E and in §3.6 (control-ID mapping in `code/regulatory_map.json`). DE.CM-09 ("personnel activity is monitored") is the most direct mapping to behavioural-analytics PAM detection in the framework.

apra_cps234_2019.author: Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA)
apra_cps234_2019.title: Prudential Standard CPS 234 — Information Security
apra_cps234_2019.notes: Cited in Appendix E as the principal Australian information-security regulatory anchor for APRA-regulated entities (banks, insurers, superannuation trustees). §27(d) controls-implementation obligation, §§30–32 incident-notification regime.

S1.claim: Sharing of privileged credentials across multiple users on a single change ticket is one of the most common credential-misuse patterns in confirmed-breach data.

citations.supports: Privilege misuse (including credential sharing and abuse of legitimate access) is a top-five action variety across breach patterns; 'human element' involvement remains in the high-60-percent range across multi-year DBIR cohorts.
Identity-based attacks (including misuse of legitimate accounts) remain the dominant initial-access vector for cloud-resident workloads.

S2.claim: Poor change-ticket justification quality is treated as a primary audit-failure indicator and is the most cited governance weakness in regulated PAM deployments.

citations.section: Insider threat chapter — Governance and process gaps
citations.supports: Documentation and audit-trail quality gaps are recurring root causes in insider-related incidents covered by NIS2 risk-management measures.
Organisations with mature incident response (which depends on auditable documentation including ticket justifications) reduce average breach cost by approximately USD 0.5-1.0 million per incident.

S3.claim: Repeated credential fetches against a single long-lived ticket extend the legitimate-access window beyond what the original change required — a known precursor to the long dwell times reported in incident-response retrospectives.

citations.section: Dwell time — Global median and regional breakdowns
citations.supports: Median attacker dwell time has compressed in recent reporting periods but remains in the multi-week range globally; insider-misuse cases skew longer because the activity blends with legitimate access.
Insider-misuse breaches consistently show longer time-to-discovery than external-actor breaches in DBIR's annual breakdowns.

S4.claim: Scope creep — using a low-friction change ticket to obtain access for work that would have required higher-friction approval if requested honestly — is one of the harder insider-misuse patterns to detect because the actor holds legitimate credentials and remains broadly within the access scope of their role.

citations.supports: Privilege Misuse is the breach pattern with the highest percentage of insider actors and the lowest percentage of malware involvement, indicating that detection signal sits in behavioural rather than malware indicators.
CISA lists 'unusual scope of work or access patterns inconsistent with stated job function' as a top behavioural indicator of insider misuse.

S5.claim: Off-hours and off-window privileged access is the most operationally-deployed time-based anomaly signal in production PAM telemetry, and one of the highest-precision early indicators in incident retrospectives.

citations.section: Core UEBA capabilities — Temporal anomaly detection
citations.supports: Time-of-day and time-of-week anomaly detection is identified as one of the foundational UEBA capabilities every vendor in the market guide ships out-of-the-box.
M-Trends consistently reports a non-uniform temporal distribution of initial-access events, with off-hours weighting for credential-driven intrusions.

S7.claim: Destructive operations executed under cover of a routine non-destructive ticket category are a recognised pattern in both insider-sabotage cases and ransomware-affiliate playbooks.

citations.supports: Mandiant catalogs destructive-attack incidents annually, with a substantial share involving misuse of legitimate accounts and tools (LotL techniques).
Destruction of data or services is one of the four primary insider-threat outcomes catalogued by CISA, alongside espionage, fraud, and unauthorised disclosure.

S10.claim: Lateral pivot to assets not authorised by the originating change ticket is one of the most reliable single-event indicators of either insider scope abuse or post-compromise adversary movement.

citations.supports: Lateral movement appears in the majority of M-Trends-tracked incidents; the most-used lateral-movement tools are legitimate administrative utilities (Living-off-the-Land).
Use of legitimate remote-access tools for unauthorised lateral access is among the top hacking-action varieties in multi-year DBIR data.

S11.claim: Continued use of a credential after the change window has explicitly closed indicates either failure of automated rotation or a parallel credential-acquisition path bypassing rotation — both of which are recurring real-world findings in PAM-product deployment retrospectives.

citations.supports: Persistence via legitimate-credential reuse remains one of the top persistence techniques observed by Mandiant across reporting years.
Detection of credential reuse beyond the issued change-window is identified as a high-value PAM/UEBA integration use case in Gartner's market guidance.

S12.claim: Reconnaissance against high-value data assets (PII columns, secret files, credential stores) without explicit ticket authorisation is one of the most directly regulator-relevant insider-misuse signals because of its intersection with GDPR Article 32 and PCI-DSS Requirement 3.

citations.supports: DBIR consistently reports that personal data is the most-frequently-affected data type across insider-driven breaches.

citations.section: Cost per compromised record by data type
citations.supports: PII and PHI carry the highest per-record breach cost in IBM's annual cost-by-data-type breakdown.

S13.claim: Use of named lateral-movement tooling (nmap, psexec, Invoke-Command, xfreerdp) inside a privileged session is one of the highest-confidence single-token indicators of post-compromise adversary behaviour or insider environment-reconnaissance.

citations.supports: Mandiant tracks LotL technique prevalence annually; remote-services and remote-system-discovery techniques (T1021, T1018) appear in a substantial fraction of investigated intrusions.
MITRE's enterprise matrix codifies 9 lateral-movement techniques and 13 sub-techniques observed in real adversary campaigns.

S14.claim: In-session privilege escalation (sudo su, chmod u+s, group-membership manipulation) is a routinely-observed step in both insider misuse and post-compromise adversary chains, particularly for hands-on-keyboard actor activity.

citations.supports: Mandiant reports privilege-escalation activity in the majority of investigated intrusions where the initial foothold was a non-administrative account.
MITRE catalogues 13 privilege-escalation techniques; Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism (T1548) and Valid Accounts (T1078) overlap heavily with the patterns this scenario covers.

S15.claim: Segregation-of-duties bypass — the same person both approving and implementing a change — is the textbook occupational-fraud control failure and the most frequently cited governance breakdown in audit findings against regulated change-management processes.

citations.section: Concealment methods and anti-fraud controls — Segregation of duties
citations.supports: ACFE consistently reports that the absence or weakness of segregation-of-duties controls is associated with substantially higher median fraud losses and longer fraud durations.
CISA lists separation of approval and implementation roles as a foundational organisational control for insider-threat mitigation.

S16.claim: Adversaries who paraphrase commands to avoid the literal trigger phrases of pattern-matching detectors are a documented, well-understood evasion technique; rule-based and signature-based detection alone is widely held to be insufficient against motivated insider or post-compromise actors who can iterate on detection responses.

citations.section: T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information — Sub-technique T1027.010 Command Obfuscation
citations.supports: MITRE catalogues command obfuscation as a recurring defence-evasion sub-technique observed across both criminal and state-aligned campaigns; SQL paraphrasing and use of stored-procedure aliases for destructive operations are documented procedural patterns under this technique family.

citations.section: Technical detection — Limitations of signature-based monitoring
citations.supports: CISA explicitly warns that pattern-matching and rule-based monitoring tools are insufficient on their own for insider threats because authorised users can adapt their actions to avoid known triggers; behavioural-analytic and machine-learning detection layers are recommended to complement them.
